subject: Polaris dedicated capacity: SLA, sizing, and one-time credit request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@polarisai.com>, Chris Taylor <ctaylor@polarisai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris dedicated capacity: initial sizing and commercial ask

Hi Sarah / Chris —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. As promised, I pulled together a preliminary dedicated-reserved proposal that aligns to the throughput profile you shared (peak bursts up to 12k tokens/s, steady at ~3k tokens/s). Attached is a draft MOU (polaris_mou_v2.pdf) plus a quick GPU sizing sheet.

High level offer:
- Reserved pool: 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent (logical pool), burst up to 12 GPUs via overflow for short windows
- Monthly committed throughput target: 2.7M tokens/day average (6-month lookback), with credits for overage tiers
- SLA: 99.5% availability for the provisioned pool; 50ms p50 token latency baseline for synchronous calls (detailed SLOs in SLA draft)

Commercial ask: Polaris is asking us to match a competitor credit they were offered (VertaCloud) — a one-time onboarding credit applied across the first 3 billing cycles. To move quickly, we can consider a one-time onboarding credit and a modest up-front discount contingent on a 12-month reserved commit. I want to loop in Marcus and Priyom internally to confirm what level of credit we can approve without exec sign-off.

Could you confirm: 1) expected minimum sustained QPS for weekdays vs weekends, 2) preferred commit term (12 vs 24 months), and 3) whether procurement will accept the draft MOU as the basis for legal redlines?

Attachments: [polaris_mou_v2.pdf (application/pdf)], [gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@polarisai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Taylor <ctaylor@polarisai.com>, procurement@polarisai.com
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris dedicated capacity: initial sizing and commercial ask

Kimberly —

Appreciate the fast follow. We reviewed the draft and attached an internal MOU note (we'll send a marked-up copy if helpful). A few clarifications from our side:

- Sustained QPS: weekdays ~3.1k tokens/s steady-state with predictable midday spikes up to 10k tokens/s for 15–30 minutes; weekends ~1.2k tokens/s.
- Term: preference for 12 months with a 12-month option to renew; we can consider 24 months if we get the competitive credit matched.
- The competitor (VertaCloud) offered a $150k one-time credit and a small SaaS discount for year one — we're not asking you to match headline-for-headline but need a commercially equivalent concession to proceed without a second procurement RFP.

We attached our internal commentary. Can your team quantify the effective cost per token under your proposed configuration? Also need to see the exact SLA language on throughput/priority routing for spikes.

Regards,
Sarah Bennett
VP of Platform Engineering, Polaris AI
sarah.bennett@polarisai.com

[Attachment: polaris_internal_comments.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Polaris dedicated capacity: initial sizing and commercial ask (internal)

Kim / Priyom —

I reviewed the numbers. We can propose the following structure to be reasonably competitive while protecting unit economics:

- Reserved pool: 8 GPUs baseline, with automatic overflow to burst pool up to 12 GPUs for 30-minute windows; intelligent routing to cheaper family GPUs for non-latency-critical workloads.
- Pricing: effective token cost target ~0.0008 USD/token at the committed volume (12-month term). We would need to layer a one-time onboarding credit of $120,000 to get the EAC within 10% of the VertaCloud offer.
- SLA wording: propose adding a throughput SLO for 'burst consistency' (95th percentile guarantees for 1-minute windows during business hours) — see attached GPU sizing sheet and SLA redline.

I flagged the $120k credit as an exception that likely requires Lauren's sign-off (legal and finance pre-approved). If we add a modest 4% discount on invoice for the first 3 months, we preserve margin and get Polaris to commit.

Attachments: [gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx], [polaris-sla-draft.docx]

-Marcus
Senior Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@polarisai.com>, Chris Taylor <ctaylor@polarisai.com>, procurement@polarisai.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Polaris dedicated capacity: initial sizing and commercial ask

Sarah / Chris —

Thanks for the details. Based on internal calibration we can put forward a firm commercial that looks like this:

- 12-month reserved commit (option to renew at 12m) for baseline 8 GPUs; burst up to 12 GPUs for short windows.
- One-time onboarding credit: $120,000 applied across first three invoices (one-time exception).
- Intro discount: additional 4% credit on invoices months 1–3.
- SLA: 99.5% availability; 50ms p50 token latency baseline; burst-consistency SLO (95th percentile 1-min windows during 09:00–18:00 PT). Full text in attached SLA draft.

We need an exec credit approval to finalize DocuSign. Marcus suggested $120k as the right balance. I'm looping in Priyom (revenue ops) and Lauren (commercial approval lead) to request exception approval. If you accept, I'll route the DocuSign and Legal will do a short redline pass.

DocuSign link (draft): https://www.docusign.net/Polaris-SLA-12345

Thanks — let me know if we should change any SLA bullets before I send to Legal.

Best,
Kimberly

[Attachments: polaris-sla-draft.docx]
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris dedicated capacity: internal approval for one-time credit

Kim / Marcus / Priyom —

Approved provisionally: we can authorize a one-time onboarding credit of $120,000 for Polaris AI, contingent on the following safeguards:
1) Signed 12-month reserved commit with a minimum monthly throughput commitment (as specified in the MOU).
2) Legal to sign off on the SLA burst-consistency language; no open indemnity gaps.
3) Finance to place the credit on a separate ledger code and require final review if any early termination occurs.

Rationale: Polaris is strategic (platform partner for two of our go-to-market references) and we are in a competitive deal cycle with VertaCloud. This amount is within my approval band for strategic closures, but I want Priyom to add a short memo to the deal record describing the commercial comp.

Loop in Legal and Finance and once they clear, Kimberly can send the DocuSign.

- Lauren Bishop
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@polarisai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Taylor <ctaylor@polarisai.com>, procurement@polarisai.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris dedicated capacity: initial sizing and commercial ask

Kimberly —

Thanks — that structure is reasonable and addresses the gap vs VertaCloud. Procurement is ready to accept the MOU once Legal confirms the SLA text. We have two quick clarifications before we sign: 1) can you confirm the guaranteed p50/p95 token latency numbers for the baseline 8-GPU pool (not burst)? 2) can the overflow burst be prioritized so our critical endpoints get routed first during contention?

If we get confirmation on those two points today, we'll route DocuSign and procurement will sign.

Best,
Sarah

On Mon, 09 Aug 2027 at 15:05:00 -0700, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sarah —
>
> Quick answers: baseline pool p50 token latency target = 50ms; p95 = 160ms for synchronous calls at typical seq lengths (see SLA table). Burst routes are prioritized by route policy: critical endpoints are pinned to high-priority queues and will be routed first; overflow to burst pool is only used after priority routing is evaluated. I will ask Legal to return redlines by EOD and trigger the DocuSign.

>
